conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's unfinished analysis section
Whether Agent D should work during/after a wake versus attend family obligations
Redistribution of workload and scheduling (who does analysis, formatting, review)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants used concrete, role-specific commitments (A: "I'll take over the analysis...", B: "I can review...", C: "I'll get it done").
D repeatedly offered to do the work then explicitly withdrew; this exchange clarified priorities (family vs. deadline).
No outside parties could help; solutions were practical redistributions rather than appeals to authority.
evaluation.final_reason: Team members agreed on a concrete redistribution: Agent A volunteered to "take over the analysis for your section" (Turn 9), Agent B agreed to "review it tomorrow afternoon" (Turn 10), Agent C committed to finish his part and then start slides (Turn 19). Agent D withdrew his offer to do the work and accepted the team's plan: "Okay, Agent A. If you're sure..." (Turn 15) and later: "I'll leave it with you all, then." (Turn 20). The incompatible demands (D insisting he do it vs. A preferring D be with family) were settled by D conceding and the team accommodating the extra work distribution.
position_change_notes: Agent D changed position: initially volunteered to complete the section himself (Turn 6, Turn 13) but later withdrew and accepted the team's plan (Turn 15, Turn 20).
Agent A held to the stance that D should be with family but adjusted practically by volunteering to take over the analysis (Turn 7 and Turn 9).
Agent B initially refused to take on more (Turn 4) but later agreed to a limited role as reviewer (Turn 10).
Agent C moved from inability to do the analysis (Turn 5) to conditional assistance after finishing his own part (Turn 12) and then provided a clear completion time (Turn 19).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent A: "I'm very sorry to hear that, Agent D." Turn 2 — Agent D: "Thanks, Agent A." (condolences; no disagreement about work)

Turn 3 — Agent A: "...you're out until Thursday. The pitch is due Thursday morning, and your section isn't finished. The three of us will have to find a way to complete it." Turn 4 — Agent B: "I can't take on more. I'm already covering for the colleague on leave." (clear disagreement begins over who will cover D's unfinished section)

Turn 5 — Agent C: "I can't do her section. I don't know that analysis, and I'm still trying to finish my own part." Turn 6 — Agent D: "I understand. I can work on it tonight when I get home. I'll send an update by morning." (several refusals but D offers a concrete solution; conflict reduced but not settled)

Turn 7 — Agent A: "I appreciate the offer, but that's not going to be reliable. You need to be with your family. We can't count on you being able to work after a wake. We need to find another way." Turn 8 — Agent D: "But I can do it. What other way is there? I have to be at the wake, and my part needs to be done." (direct, opposing positions about whether D should attempt the work)

Turn 9 — Agent A: "Okay, here's another way. I'll take over the analysis for your section. Agent C... help with the slide formatting and sourcing data? Agent B... could you review it tomorrow?" Turn 10 — Agent B: "Okay. I can review it tomorrow afternoon." (a concrete redistribution is proposed and partially accepted; some coordination unresolved)
Turn 11 — Agent A: "Agent C, what about you?" Turn 12 — Agent C: "I can, but I need to finish my part first. I'm still behind on it." (conditional agreement; minor remaining scheduling risk)

Turn 13 — Agent D: "Agent A, that's a lot for you to take on, and Agent C needs to finish his part first. Let me just do it tonight. I can get it done. It's less risk." Turn 14 — Agent A: "No, Agent D. It's a bigger risk to count on you working tonight after a wake. We will manage. You go be with your family." (conflict reappears between A and D over who should do the work)

Turn 15 — Agent D: "Okay, Agent A. If you're sure. I am worried about the extra work for you..." Turn 17 — Agent C: "Don't worry about my part. I'll get it done." (D withdraws his offer; team plan accepted and C commits to finishing his part — incompatibility settled)

Turn 18 — Agent A: "Okay, but when do you think you'll be done with your part?" Turn 19 — Agent C: "I should be done by tomorrow morning. I'll start on the slides right after." (scheduling clarification; no disagreement)
Turn 20 — Agent D: "Okay. Thank you, everyone. I'll leave it with you all, then." Turn 21 — Agent A: "Take care, Agent D. We'll handle it." (mutual closure; no outstanding dispute)

substantive_insights: Primary tension was between D's desire/ability to finish the work vs. A's assessment that D should prioritize family; this is a duty-to-family vs. duty-to-deadline tradeoff.
Resolution relied on redistributing labor among available team members with conditional timing (C helps after finishing his part; B only reviews).
Timing constraints (C being behind and needing to finish his part first) were the main remaining operational risk until resolved by C's committed schedule.
